evidence.label: Filtered products and boundary-preserving compression in complex cobordism
Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension

headline: Claims the radius of comparison of a minimal crossed product is half the mean dimension, the Phillips–Toms conjecture.
scope: Minimal homeomorphisms of infinite compact metrizable spaces and their crossed-product C*-algebras; the companion paper proves the topological compression input.
plain: Mean dimension measures how many dimensions a dynamical system uses per time step. The radius of comparison measures how far the related operator algebra is from comparing elements by size alone. Phillips and Toms conjectured that the second is exactly half the first. This paper claims to prove it for every minimal homeomorphism, using a companion paper on maps into cubes. There is no Lean check.
doesNot: This does not cover actions of groups other than the integers, which the broader form of the conjecture includes.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Toms, who introduced the radius of comparison (Definition 6.1)
scorecard.significanceWhy: It would settle the integer-action case of the Phillips–Toms conjecture, listed as Problem XXXVI in a recent survey.

explanation:
Cover the interval [0, 1] by two open pieces, [0, 0.6) and (0.4, 1]. At most two pieces overlap at any point. The order of the cover is one less than that, so it is 1. No cover of the interval by small pieces can do better, which is why its dimension is 1. A square needs points where three pieces meet, so its dimension is 2.

Now let a map h move the points of a space X, one step per unit of time. Mean dimension asks how much dimension the system uses per step[3]. Refine a cover by following each point for N steps, take the order of that refined cover, and divide by N. Gromov introduced mean dimension, and Lindenstrauss and Weiss developed it[4]. It stays finite for some systems on infinite-dimensional spaces. A homeomorphism is minimal when every orbit comes close to every point.

Each such system gives a C*-algebra, the crossed product, built from functions on X and one operator for the map. In nice algebras, one positive element sits below another whenever its size under every trace is smaller. Toms's radius of comparison measures the extra margin needed for that to work[5]. The Phillips–Toms conjecture says the radius equals half the mean dimension. The half is suggested by how complex rank relates to real dimension: one complex direction is two real ones. Phillips proved the radius is at most 1 + 36 times the mean dimension[10]. Niu proved the sharp upper bound of one half[6]. For mean dimension 2, Phillips's bound gives 73, and Niu's gives 1. The obstacle was the matching lower bound.

The paper claims the conjecture for every minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space[1]. This includes the case where both sides are infinite. It follows that zero mean dimension is equivalent to Jiang–Su stability and to finite nuclear dimension, two key regularity properties[2]. The proof assumes the cover rate is more than twice a comparison bound, then turns comparison into a bundle embedding. A bundle is a family of vector spaces over a space. The companion paper supplies the step that pushes maps into cubes onto cube boundaries[7]. It needs the bundle's target rank to be less than twice the source rank[8]. An example at equality shows this strict inequality cannot be removed[9]. The compressed maps give a smaller cover, which is a contradiction.

How sure is this? There is no Lean check. A computer proof checker has not looked at any part of it. The proof spans two long papers, one in stable homotopy theory. No specialist review is published.
hypeCheck: Major if correct: it claims an exact formula conjectured by Phillips and Toms. There is no Lean check and no published specialist review.

glossary.meaning: One less than the largest number of pieces of an open cover that share a common point.
The growth rate, per time step, of the order needed to cover a dynamical system's orbit segments.
A continuous invertible map whose every orbit comes arbitrarily close to every point.
A C*-algebra built from the functions on a space and one operator implementing the map.
The smallest margin r such that trace size plus r always decides when one positive element sits below another.
An algebra A with A ⊗ Z isomorphic to A, a key regularity property in classification.
A noncommutative version of covering dimension, defined by finite-dimensional approximations.
A tool from stable homotopy theory that detects when a map can be deformed to a constant.

claims.text: For every minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space, the radius of comparison of its crossed product equals half its mean dimension.
claims.sourceLine: the radius of comparison of its crossed product equals one half of its
claims.sourceQuote: We prove the integer-action case of the Phillips--Toms conjecture: for every minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space, the radius of comparison of its crossed product equals one half of its mean dimension, including equality at infinity.

claims.text: Zero mean dimension and the small boundary property are equivalent to Jiang–Su stability and finite nuclear dimension of the crossed product.

claims.sourceQuote: For these systems, zero mean dimension and the small boundary property are equivalent to Jiang--Su stability and to finite nuclear dimension of the crossed product; in this case its nuclear dimension is at most one.

claims.sourceQuote: When the torus slot bundle embeds continuously into a trivial bundle of rank less than twice the source rank, the compression places a positive proportion of slots on their boundaries in arbitrarily large powers and fixes every original boundary slot exactly.
